eddied.needs: 1 usable QB (Brock Purdy) for 1 starting slot; 2 usable RB (Zach Charbonnet, Breece Hall) for 1 starting slot; 1 usable WR (Malik Nabers) for 1 starting slot; 1 usable TE (Brock Bowers) for 1 starting slot; 1 usable DL (George Karlaftis) for 1 starting slot; 4 usable LB for 1 starting slot; 3 usable DB for 2 starting slots. DL is short of the depth bar (1 usable, bar 2).

method.offense: Offensive ROS points = per-game rate times games left from week 10 through week 17, minus one if that NFL bye is still ahead. The rate is the week-board consensus in data/rankings (Wheels Up points). A bye or a blank consensus uses last-3 actuals from that file. If the player is missing there, the rate is data/player-values.json ppg times 0.90, the median ratio of the week-8 board to that older file. There is no separate offensive ROS rank file.
method.idp: IDP ROS points are rosPts from data/idp-rankings.json (week 10, byes already zeroed in that file). That file is a top cut, so a rostered IDP missing from it uses player-values ppg times 0.90 times games left when that rate is at least 8. An active IDP in neither file is a flat 100 ROS (a body, so a missing rank is not an empty room). A reserve IDP in neither file is 50.
method.injury: IR, Out, PUP, NFI, and suspended are 0. Achilles or ACL text is 0.15. Doubtful is 0.35. Questionable is 0.90. An IDP the rankings file already tagged is not discounted twice. Edgerrin Cooper and Tremaine Edmunds are season-ending and are left out of every side.
method.valueDelta: Eddies' optimized lineup rest-of-season points after the swap, minus before. The lineup is 65% healthy, 25% with Breece Hall sitting, 10% with George Karlaftis sitting, so RB depth and a second DL count even when the healthy lineup is already full. partnerDelta is the other club's healthy lineup, same slots, no injury-risk weight.
method.fit: Fit is 0-100. Incoming targets are RB, DL, LB, and DB. The other club must be deep at that spot (3+ usable RBs, 3+ usable DLs, 3+ usable LBs, 3+ usable DBs) and the idea never asks for their best one. An offense-for-IDP 2-for-1 is allowed. Giving offense back for offense is allowed when the other bars clear; it is a guideline, not a filter. The piece the Eddies send has to fill a thin IDP spot (fewer than 2 usable LBs or DLs, or fewer than 3 usable DBs) or a thin WR room, or it has to start for them. Their lineup can drop at most 12 points when that piece starts for them or fills a real hole. Eddies need at least 3 blended points, and giving up someone who is in the healthy lineup has to leave that healthy lineup ahead too. A spot where the Eddies are under the depth bar scores a bit higher. Bench surplus scores a bit higher than a starter. A name already on a trade block scores higher. Jordyn Brooks, Cedric Gray, and Josh Downs are never outgoing.
method.lineup: 1 QB, 1 RB, 1 WR, 1 TE, 3 RB/WR/TE, 1 DL, 1 LB, 2 DB, 3 IDP. Greedy, same slots as the trade tab.

notes: Each idea stands on its own. Making one would change the rest of the board.
No idea brings back a defensive back. No spare DB cleared the fit bar (a deep room, not their best player, and both lineups).
